_note: Tracked cross-unit threads. Per-thread shape (matches Matthew's data/threads.json): id, root, translit, gloss, example? (one quoted in-text usage, plain voice, no citations -- style reference §1, only when it clarifies the translation choice), color, status ('open'/'closed'), tagged (bool), opens {unit, ref}, payoffs [{unit, ref, note?}], note (prose). Each thread's `root` must also resolve to an entry in data/roots.json (a hand-curated set of Strong's/lemma ids, see pipeline/roots.py) before pipeline/audit_thread_coverage.py can audit it. candidates/retro are NOT thread.json fields -- those live per-unit in a fragment's unit-meta block (threads.candidates/threads.retro), see pipeline/unit_meta.py's module docstring. Promotion policy (2026-09-16, Lane): Claude decides book-wide vs. local per unit, biased toward book-wide (a thread kept local when payoff shows up later is worse than one tracked that never pays off); Claude asks Lane only when genuinely unsure. `payoffs` stays empty until the unit containing the payoff is actually built -- don't cite a ref in an unbuilt unit.

opens.note: natan ×8 in unit 1's speeches; Yahweh 'is giving' (participle) vs. 'Moses gave' (perfect) — the land as gift, already done and not yet done.

payoffs.note: The first voice after Yahweh's to say the land is already given is a Canaanite prostitute's — the gift confirmed from the far side of the wall.
The spies' whole report is Rahab's sentence handed back to Joshua: Yahweh has given the land into our hand.

threads.note: natan ×8 in unit 1's speeches; Yahweh 'is giving' (participle) vs. 'Moses gave' (perfect) — the land as gift, already done and not yet done.

threads.gloss: cross over; the far side (of the Jordan)

opens.note: the book's first command, qum ʿavor 'rise, cross' (1:2), relayed down the chain (1:11); ʿever 'far side' marks the eastern tribes as people of the other bank. One root, both ids.

payoffs.note: ʿever, 'the far side of the Jordan' — spoken from Jericho's bank, Sihon and Og are the ones across the river.
Two men cross the Jordan ahead of the nation — a small, secret crossing before the great public one of unit 3.

threads.note: Oaths bind the book together: Yahweh's oath to the fathers (1:6), Rahab's oath (2:12, 17, 20), its keeping (6:22), the Gibeonite oath (9:15, 19-20), the rest formula (21:43-44).

threads.note: Melting hearts: Rahab's 'our heart melted' (2:11) returns for the Amorite and Canaanite kings (5:1) and, reversed, for Israel after Ai (7:5).
